Neuropeptide Y and neuron-specific enolase levels in benign and malignant pheochromocytomas.  
Neuron-specific enolase (NSE) is the isoform of enolase, a glycolytic enzyme present in the neuroendocrine system.  
Neuropeptide Y (NPY) is a recently discovered peptide in the peripheral and central nervous systems.  
Serum NSE and plasma NPY levels have been reported to be increased in some patients with pheochromocytom.  
The authors assessed whether measuring these molecules could help discriminate between benign and malignant forms of pheochromocytom.  
NSE levels were normal in all patients with benign pheochromocytom (n = 13) and elevated in half of patients with malignant pheochromocytom (n = 13).  
Plasma NPY levels were on average significantly higher in malignant forms (177.1 +/- 38.9 pmol/l, n = 16) than in benign forms of the disease (15.7 +/- 389 pmol/l, n = 24).  
However, there was no difference in the percentage of patients with elevated NPY levels.  
These results show that the determination of serum NSE can be useful in distinguishing malignant and benign pheochromocytoma; measuring plasma NPY is not useful in differentiating the two types of tumors.

Sexually transmitted diseases of the colon, rectum and anus.  
The challenge of the 90s.  
Over the past two decades, there has been an explosive growth in the prevalence and types of sexually transmitted diseases.  
Up to 55 percent of gay men with anorectal disorders have gonorrhea; 80 percent of syphylis patients are homosexuals.  
Chlamydiia is present in 15 percent of asymptomatic gay men, and up to a third of gay men have active anorectal herpes simplex virus.  
Additionally, a multitude of parasites, bacterial, viral and protozoan, all plague the homosexual population.  
Additionally, the global AIDS epidemic has produced a plethora of colorectal manifestations.  
Acute cytomegalovirus ileocolitis is the most common indication for emergency abdominal surgery in homosexual men with AIDS.  
In addition to cryptosporidis and isospores, the patient may present to the colorectal surgeon with bloody diarrhea and weight loss before the diagnosis of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) disease.  
Other patients may have Kaposi's colorectal sarcoma or anorectal lymphoma and will therefore be HIV positive.  
However, in addition to these protean manifestations, a third of AIDS patients consult the colorectal surgeon either for condyloma acuminatum, or for anorectal septicemia, or for proctitis before the diagnosis of HIV disease.  
Although aggressive anorectal surgery is associated with reasonable surgical outcomes in some asymptomatic HIV-positive patients, the same procedures in AIDS patients (symptomatic HIV-positive) will often produce disastrous results.  
It is therefore the responsibility of the surgeon to recognize the manifestations of HIV disease and to diagnose these conditions accordingly.

The identification of carotid restenosis as an unexpected late complication of carotid endarterectomy has raised concerns about its significance as a source of new stroke symptoms, strokes, and death.
To investigate these concerns, we analyzed a consecutive series of 507 patients undergoing 566 carotid endarterectomies, each documented as technically satisfactory.
Data from postoperative duplex Doppler examination at 3 days, 1, 3, 6, 12 months, then annually in 484 arteries (85.5%) made it possible to classify these arteries according to the most severe degree of postoperative severity: normal (n = 306); 1% to 19% (n = 89); 20% to 50% (n = 40); more than 50% (n = 49, including 8 occluded).
The incidence of restenosis greater than 50% was 14.5% in women and 7.7% in men (p = 0.003).

Thus, patients with carotid restenosis were less likely than patients with normal postoperative examinations to experience late symptoms, stroke, or early death.

source: Pharmacomechanical thrombolysis and angioplasty in the management of coagulated hemodialysis grafts: early and late clinical results. The results of pharmacomechanical thrombolysis and angioplasty of 121 thrombosed hemodialysis grafts were examined. The initial pharmacomechanical method (used in 65 cases) used maceration of the clot with hook-shaped catheters and lacing of the clot with highly concentrated urokinase. The current technique (used in 56 cases) consisted of a pulsed spray injection of urokinase into the clot. All fully treated grafts (117 cases) underwent complete or near-complete thrombolysis, and 93% remained patent after 1 day. The average pulse spray lysis time was 46 minutes +/- 21. One patient (less than 1%) had gastrointestinal hemorrhage and received a transfusion; minor complications occurred in 3% of patients. The primary and secondary graft patency rates for the two methods at 1 year were 26% and 51%, respectively. Although graft age and angioplasty outcomes did not influence future graft patency, shorter intervals between graft thromboses were predictive of subsequent graft failure. The results suggest that pharmacomechanical thrombolysis and angioplasty enable rapid, consistent, and safe recanalization of coagulated hemodialysis grafts and represent a promising additional therapeutic approach for long-term graft management.

Color Doppler diagnosis of mechanical prosthetic mitral regurgitation: usefulness of the flow convergence region proximal to the regurgitant orifice.  
In prosthetic or paravalvular mitral regurgitation, transthoracic color Doppler flow mapping may sometimes fail to detect the regurgitant jet in the left atrium due to shadowing of the prosthetic valve.  
To overcome this limitation, we evaluated the utility of color Doppler visualization of the flow convergence region (FCR) proximal to the regurgitant orifice in 20 consecutive patients with mechanical prosthetic mitral regurgitation documented by surgery and cardiac catheterization (13 of 20 patients).  
In addition, we studied 33 patients with normally functioning mitral prostheses.  
Doppler studies were performed in the apical, subcostal, and parasternal long-axis views.  
FCR was detected in 95% (19 of 20) of patients with prosthetic mitral regurgitation.  
A jet zone in the left was detected in 60% (12 of 20) of patients.  
In 18 of 19 patients with Doppler-detected FCR, the leak site was correctly identified by observing the location of the FCR.  
A trivial jet zone was detected in eight patients with a normally functioning mitral prosthesis; no FCR was identified.  
Thus, color Doppler visualization of the FCR proximal to the regurgitant orifice is superior to the jet zone in the diagnosis of mechanical prosthetic mitral regurgitation.  
In addition, the FCR makes it possible to locate the leak site with good precision.

source: Sodium-sensitive hypertension and sodium retention. The differences between sodium-sensitive hypertension and sodium-sensitive hypertension were theoretically examined using a water reservoir model of regulation of body fluid volume and blood pressure. If an outlet valve is attached to a reservoir whose base area is the reciprocal of the total peripheral resistance (TPR) and water is poured into that reservoir at a rate corresponding to the amount of Na+ absorbed, then equilibrium must be achieved at a certain water level, volume, and flow rate of the outlet, which represent mean arterial pressure (MAP), cardiac output (CO), and urinary excretion of Na+. The height of the outlet from the bottom of the tank and the size of the cross section of the outlet correspond respectively to the ordinate at the origin and the slope of the renal function curve (pressure-natriurese). In sodium-retaining hypertension, due to the shift of the curve to a higher blood pressure level (higher outlet size) without changing the slope (outlet size), and in sodium-sensitive hypertension, due to the lowered slope of the curve (reduced outlet size), not only the MAP (water level) but also the CO (water volume) are increased, resulting in sodium-retaining hypertension, if the TPR (inverse of baseline surface area) remains unchanged, while CO is relatively unchanged, resulting in non-sodium hypertension. maintain hypertension, if the TPR is high. Thus, MAP and its sensitivity to sodium intake are determined by the renal function curve. Because body fluid volume is determined by both the renal function curve and the TPR, changes in TPR during the development of hypertension are a major factor in determining whether or not body fluid volume should change only a small amount or a large amount. Therefore, sodium sensitivity of blood pressure and sodium retention must be considered separately.

source: Usefulness of frozen section lymph node assessment in the staging of bronchogenic carcinoma during mediastinoscopy and thoracotomy. We conducted a retrospective analysis of the usefulness of frozen section diagnostics in determining lymph node status at mediastinoscopy in 122 consecutive patients with bronchogenic carcinoma. Thirty-five of 122 patients had one or more lymph nodes with frozen section evaluation positive for metastatic carcinoma. Subsequent lymph node sections not included in the original frozen section study revealed metastatic carcinoma in two additional patients. The false negative rate was 1.6%. The sensitivity was 94.6%. The predictive value of negative results from the evaluation of frozen sections was 97.7%. As there were no false-positive frozen section results, the specificity and predictive value of positive frozen section results was 100%. The status of individual lymph nodes in these 122 patients was also evaluated. Six hundred and twenty lymph nodes were collected from the mediastinum during mediastinoscopy. Frozen sections of 47 lymph nodes were positive. Subsequent lymph node sections not included in the initial frozen section examination revealed metastatic carcinoma in four additional lymph nodes. The false negative rate was 0.6%. The sensitivity was 92.2%. The predictive value of negative results from the evaluation of frozen sections was 99.3%. As there were no false-positive frozen section results, the specificity and predictive value of positive frozen section results were 100%. We conclude that evaluation of lymph nodes by frozen section during mediastinoscopy reliably indicates the status of the lymph nodes, thus allowing the physician to proceed or not to perform thoracotomy. Thus, carcinoma staging and definitive surgery can be performed during a single anesthetic procedure. The combination of mediastinoscopy and thoracotomy with frozen section diagnostic monitoring also reduces both the length and cost of hospitalization.

source: In vitro and in vivo effects in the coronary sinus of non-arc and arc shocks using a novel low-energy DC ablation system. DC shocks within the coronary sinus have been abandoned due to the risk of cardiac rupture and tamponade. Catheter ablation using DC energy on electrodes straddling the coronary sinus ostium, when used clinically, has been reported to result in cardiac tamponade in up to 16% of patients. A new energy distribution system maximizes tension while reducing unwanted effects caused by barotrauma. This system includes 1) a low energy ablation electrical power supply with a brief capacitive discharge constant over time which delivers up to 40 J and 3000 V and 2) a low energy ablation catheter with a profiled distal electrode. We carried out in vitro and in vivo studies of this new system and compared shocks with arc and shocks without arc. In vitro studies were carried out in a large air tank filled with physiological saline solution while recording voltage, current and pressure. High-speed cinematography (32,000 images/sec) of shocks from 10 to 40 J allowed a detailed analysis of the vapor globe. Anodal shocks of less than 20 J showed no electric arcing or only minimal formation of vapor globes. For the D and P-D anodal shocks of 40 J, the vapor globe diameters were 31 and 22 mm, respectively, corresponding to pressure records of 11 and 4.9 atm. The pressure build-up lasted less than 50 mu ss. The in vivo studies involved 18 dogs that received shocks without an arc (one to six shocks of 15 J) and 18 dogs that received shocks with an arc (one to three shocks of 40 J). Each group was divided between shocks D and P-D; Catheter ablation was performed at a mean distance +/- SEM of 2.94 +/- 0.92 cm in the coronary sinus. All dogs tolerated the procedure without cardiac rupture or tamponade. When killed 2 to 4 days later, the dogs showed edema and hyperemia or hemorrhage in the sinus coronari. We compared the effects of several (three to six) non-arc shocks with the effects of one to three arc shocks. Disturbance or rupture of the sinus coronari into the epicardial fat space occurred in two of 12 dogs (17%) with multiple nonarc shocks, but in 13 of 18 dogs (72%) with arc shocks (p less than 0.003). Sinus coronari occlusion occurred in two of 12 dogs (17%) with multiple non-arc shocks and in nine of 18 dogs (50%) with arc shocks (p less than 0.06).

To further explore the pathogenesis of glucose intolerance and insulin resistance observed in patients with cirrhosis and portal hypertension, we studied a 35-year-old woman with presinusoidal portal hypertension without cirrhosis due to nodular regenerative hyperplasia of the liver. 
After oral ingestion of glucose, glucose tolerance remained normal; however, this occurred at the expense of a markedly hyperinsulinaemic plasma response, suggesting the presence of insulin resistance. 
To examine this question more directly, we performed a stepwise euglycemic insulin clamp study in combination with [6-3H]glucose and [1-14C]palmitate infusion and indirect calorimetry. 
The ability of insulin to promote glucose absorption throughout the body (mainly muscle) was markedly impaired, while its effect of suppressing hepatic glucose production was normal compared to results obtained in nine healthy subjects. 
Furthermore, insulin failed to normally suppress plasma free fatty acid turnover and oxidation in this patient. 
This informative case demonstrates that portal hypertension alone, without hepatic dysfunction due to cirrhosis, is associated with impaired insulin-induced plasma glucose and free fatty acid metabolism and may also play a predominant role in the development of insulin resistance in many cirrhotic patients.

The aim of this study was to establish the relationship between the results of the history, physical examination, chest radiography and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP).  
PATIENTS AND METHODS: Fifty-two consecutive patients with chronic congestive heart failure, referred for evaluation for cardiac transplantation, were studied; All patients underwent history taking, physical examination, vertical chest x-ray, and cardiac catheterization.  
The mean left ventricular ejection fracton was 0.19 +/- 0.06.  
The patient was divided into three groups according to their PCWP: Group 1, normal PCWP (less than or equal to 15 mm Hg, n = 19); Group 2, mild to moderately elevated PCWP (16 to 29 mm Hg, n = 15); Group 3, notably elevated PCWP (greater than or equal to 30 mm Hg, n = 18).  
RESULTS: Physical and radiographic signs of congestion were more common in groups with higher PCWP, but they could not be used to reliably separate patients with different filling pressures.  
Physical signs (orthopnea, edema, rales, third heart sound, elevated jugular venous pressure) or radiographic signs (cardiomegaly, vascular redistribution and interstitial and alveolar edema) had a low predictive value for identifying patients with PCWP values greater than or equal to 30 mm Hg.  
These results had a low negative predictive value to exclude significantly elevated PCWP (greater than 20 mm Hg).  
Radiographic pulmonary congestion was absent in eight (53%) patients in group 2 and seven (39%) in group 3.  
In patients in groups 2 and 3, those without radiographic congestion were in a better New York Heart Association functional class (3.5 +/- 0.5 versus 2.8 +/- 0.6, p less than 0.01).  
There was a good correlation between right atrial pressure and PCWP (r = 0.64, p less than 0.001).  
Normal right atrial pressure had no predictive value, but a pressure greater than 10 mm Hg was observed in all but one patient with a PCWP value greater than 20 mm Hg.  
CONCLUSION: Clinical, radiographic and hemodynamic evaluations of chronic congestive heart failure provide contradictory results.  
The absence of radiographic or physical signs of congestion does not guarantee normal PCWP values ​​and may lead to inaccurate diagnosis and inappropriate treatment.  
It is unclear whether treatment aimed at normalizing PCWP is superior to alleviating clinical and radiographic signs of congestion.

source: Metabolic consequences of “washed” cardiopulmonary bypass pump priming fluid in children undergoing cardiac operations. The substrate load of the pump priming fluid, particularly glucose and lactate, has a major influence on the metabolic response of children during cardiac operations and can be neurologically detrimental. It is possible to clean the priming fluid from these excess substrates by ultrafiltarion followed by the addition of a balanced electrolyte solution. We used this technique in the management of bypass surgery in nine children over one year old and weighing less than 18 kg who were studied from the induction of anesthesia until 6 hours postoperatively. Frequent blood samples were taken to measure electrolytes, intermediate metabolites, and stress-related hormones. Throughout the study period, electrolyte concentrations were maintained within physiological limits and changes in blood glucose and lactate were minimized compared to those in matched historical controls from previous studies. During the body circulation period, mean serum glucose concentrations varied between 4.4 and 7.7 mmol/L and peaked at 10.7 mmol/L just before skin closure. The mean serum lactate concentration did not exceed 2.3 mmol/L during the period. Thus, ultrafiltration of the priming fluid and replacement with a balanced electrolyte solution results in the administration of a reasonably physiologic substrate load to the patient, which is reflected in improved control of average plasma intermediate metabolite concentrations. The method could serve as a basis for further clinical studies aimed at determining specific aspects of the metabolic response to stress in children.

source: Overdose of reperfusion of cardioplegic blood solution. A preventable cause of post-ischemic myocardial depression. Reperfusion of warm blood fluid is useful in minimizing reperfusion damage after ischemy. This study tests the hypothesis that overzealous administration of cardioplegic blood fluid during reperfusion counteracts these benefits and may lead to a prevalence of depressed ventricular performance and mortality similar to that observed after normal blood reperfusion. Thirty-one dogs underwent global ischemy at 37°C for 45 minutes on a ventilated bypass. Six received normal blood reperfusion and 25 were reperfused with warm cardioplegic blood solution enriched with aspartate/glutamate; of these, eight received a high dose (3,600 +/- 600 ml) and 17 received limited-dose cardioplegic blood reperfusion (1,180 +/- 120 ml) over a period of 10 to 20 minutes. High-dose cardioplegic blood perfusion (5,100 +/- 200 ml) without prior ischemistry was tested in five additional dogs. High-dose blood cardioplegia without prior ischemy did not impair ventricular function (stroke peak work index 96% of control). After ischemia, normal blood reperfusion (no cardioplegia) resulted in marked left ventricular dysfunction (peak stroke work index 36% of control, p less than 0.05 compared to control) and a mortality rate of 33% (2/6 died). High-dose cardioplegic reperfusion resulted in marginal recovery of stroke work index (40% of control, p less than 0.05 vs. control) and a mortality rate of 25% (2/8 died). In contrast, reperfusion with a limited dose of cardioplegic blood solution allowed 100% survival (17/17) and restored the stroke work index to 90% of control (1.3 versus 1.45 gm.m/kg). We conclude that reperfusion damage can be avoided by initial reoxygenation with limited doses of substrate-enriched cardioplegic blood solution. Conversely, high-dose reperfusion of cardioplegic blood fluid negates this benefit, significantly reduces recovery, and can be fatal.

source: Observations on the pathophysiology of Nelson syndrome: about three cases. Nelson syndrome is generally considered an unusual sequela of primary bilateral adrenalectomy when performed for Cushig's disease. It is classically defined by skin hyperpigmentation, significantly elevated adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) levels, and enlargement of the sella turcica. In this report, we present three cases initially treated by transsphenoidal sellar exploration for Cushing's disease. In two of these cases, remission of hypercortisolism did not occur after initial pituitary exploration. A microadenectomy was performed in one case and in the other no microadenoma was found. In both cases, Nelson syndrome occurred after adrenalectomy. A second transsphenoidal operation and radiotherapy were necessary to control tumor growth. In another case, transsphenoidal adenectomy of an ACTH-secreting tumor initially led to remission of hypercortisolism for 4 years, but recurrent Cushing's disease required adrenalectomy, and again Nelson syndrome occurred. Documentation of a pre-existing ACTH-secreting basophilic pituitary microadenoma before adrenalectomy, as observed in two of our cases, has not been reported previously, and these observations of “non-classical” developments have major implications for the pathophysiology of Nelson syndrome.

source: Occult cancer in patients with deep venous thrombosis. A systematic approach. The authors prospectively studied 113 consecutive patients with deep venous thrombosis of the lower limbs to determine the most appropriate work-up study to search for hidden cancer. After careful physical examination, the following routine tests were performed: erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), total blood count, biochemistry, carcinoembryonic antigen level, chest X-ray, upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, abdominal ultrasound, and computed tomography (CT). If a malignant lesion was suspected, other appropriate studies were performed. After discharge, periodic follow-up was carried out on all patients in the outpatient clinic. A malignant tumor was detected in 12 patients. Among these 12 patients, six were asymptomatic with the exception of one thrombophlebitis. Cancer was observed more frequently in patients with idiopathic deep vein thrombosis (DVT) (7 of 31 patients versus 5 of 82 patients with secondary DVT; P = 0.012) and in patients with abnormal lactic dehydrogenase (LDH) levels (6 of 23 versus 6 of 90; P = 0.007). Abnormal CEA levels allowed the diagnosis of two cases of colon cancer (by colonoscopy). Ultrasound and CT scan of the abdomen showed two cases of bladder carcinoma at a very early stage. In addition, two cases of adenomatous polyps in the colon were discovered, a pathology considered by most authors to be a precursor of colorectal cancer. Additionally, there were five patients with large benign pelvic tumors and two patients with absent inferior vena cava. The most striking result is that some cases of cancer are at a very early stage. It was concluded that blood counts, LDH, CEA, chest radiographs and abdominal ultrasound (or CT scan) should be routinely performed in all patients with deep vein thrombosis (especially those with idiopathic DVT). Histological evidence suggests that drugs acting as noncompetitive antagonists of the N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor may have beneficial or pathological effects on central nervous system neurons. Additional injections were administered on postoperative days 2, 4, and 6. Behavioral testing measured somatosensory asymmetries (i.e., bilateral tactile stimulation testing) and forelimb placement. After lesions of the sensorimotor cortex, rats presented an ipsilateral somatosensory bias and a deficiency in the positioning of the contralateral forelimb. Rats treated with MK-801 recovered slightly faster than animals treated with saline, as measured by a bilateral tactile stimulation test (p less than 0.05). source: The importance of cytogenetic studies in adult acute lymphocytic leukemia. OBJECTIVE: The prognostic significance of pretreatment bone marrow cytogenetic studies in adults with acute lymphocytic leukemia treated at a single institution, with an identical treatment schedule, is described. PATIENTS AND METHODS: A total of 105 patients with a documented diagnosis of acute lymphocytic leukemia were examined for this analysis. All patients underwent a thorough workup at presentation and cytogenetic analysis was performed in 103 patients, using the Giemma strip technique with trypsin pretreatment on cells in 24-hour culture. RESULTS: The specific cytogenetic classification in the 103 patients who had the karyotypic analysis was as follows: diploid 27%; Philadelphia chromosome positive 13%; hyperdiploid 12%; B cell karyotip 6%; 6q- and 14q+ anomalies 4%; pseudodiploid 8%; hypodiploid 2%; and insufficient metaphases 28%. Karyotes positive for B cells, 6q- or 14q+, and the Philadelphia chromosome tended to be correlated with other known negative prognostic factors. Patients with diploid, hyperdiploid, pseudodiploid and hypodiploid or with insufficient metaphases could be grouped into a single group with a favorable prognosis. In this group, the remission rate with induction chemotherapy was 89%, the median duration of complete remission was 26 months and the median survival was 25 months, with a 3-year survival rate of 45%. Patients with positive Philadelfia chromosome, B cell, and 6q- or 14q+ abnormalities collectively had an unfavorable prognosis. Their response rate to induction chemotherapy was 65%, the median duration of response was 7 months and the median survival was 8 months, with a 3-year survival rate greater than 10%. CONCLUSION: We conclude that pretreatment bone marrow karyotyping is an important part of the evaluation of adults with acute lymphocytic leukemia and provides meaningful prognostic information.

source: Smooth muscle cell proliferation and restenosis after autonomous coronary excimer laser angioplasty Excimer laser coronary angioplasty has been shown to remove atherosclerotic intracoronary tissue. Autonomous coronary angioplasty with excimer laser was successfully performed in a 53-year-old white man with 90% stenosis of the left anterior descending coronary artery and exertional angina (Canadian Cardiovascular Society class III). The lesion was reduced to a residual stenosis of 30% using a 1.2 mm then 1.8 mm diameter laser catheter. Early follow-up angiography 24 hours later revealed persistent patency and unchanged lesion diameter of the target vessel. The patient was asymptomatic during the 2-month follow-up period, but died suddenly while playing in a tennis tournament 63 days after surgery. Post-mortem histological examination revealed 80% restenosis at the site of the lesion without plaque rupture or thrombosis. Specific staining of the histological sample for smooth muscle cells using alpha-actin revealed significant proliferation of smooth muscle cells at the site of coronary excimer laser angioplasty. However, most of the vessel narrowing appeared to be due to underlying fibrous plaque resulting from insufficient tissue ablation. This was likely related to the size of currently available catheters, which are too small to create a large channel.

source: Late effects of treatment for Wilms tumor. A report from the National Wilms Tumor Study Group. The National Wilms' Tumor Study (NWTS) was launched in 1969. One of its objectives was to modulate treatments according to risk factors in order to minimize the number and severity of short- and long-term iatrogenic complications related to treatment. The NWTS therefore incorporated a long-term follow-up study (LTFS) into its framework to monitor late effects. The LTFS is limited to relapse-free survivors living 5 years or more after initial surgery, and data are collected using specially designed forms. A total of 787 patients enrolled in NWTS-1 or NWTS-2 (1969 to 1979) were eligible, of whom 680 (86%) were available for analysis regarding their musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, and neuropsychological status, as well as the presence of benign and malignant tumors. Patients with early-stage disease treated with radiation therapy experienced scoliosis, along with other musculoskeletal abnormalities (32 versus 2), almost seven times more often than members of the cohort population who did not receive radiation therapy (35 of 57 versus 5 of 53, respectively). The difference in cardiovascular problems among survivors who did or did not receive Adriamycin (Adria Laboratories, Columbus, OH) (2.4 versus 1.1 per 100 person-years at risk) was of limited statistical significance (P = 0.06). No excess neuropsychological events were reported in people who received the neurotoxin vincristine. When considering patients with disease at all stages, the second 5 malignancies occurred in all 623 patients who underwent radiotherapy (RT patients); benign tumors were also more common in RT patients than in patients who did not receive radiotherapy (41 of 486 or 8% versus 4 of 194 or 2%). Continued study of this unique patient body is necessary, particularly for those receiving Adriamycin, due to the known long interval required for latent cardiomyopathy to manifest clinically in some patients.

Diagnosis of oral hairy leukoplakia by ultrastructural examination of exfoliative cytological samples.  
Lingual exfoliative cytology samples (scrapings) were obtained from 18 human immunodeficiency virus-positive patients with clinical oral hairy leukoplakia.  
Scrapings of the oral mucosa were obtained in 12 of these patients.  
The specimens were processed for examination by transmission electron microscopy (TEM).  
Sixteen (89%) of the lingual samples revealed infection of keratinocytes with a herpes-like virus.  
There was no evidence of viral infection in the 12 oral mucosal scrapings.  
Fungal hyphae were observed by TEM in 14 (78%) of the lingual scrapings and two (17%) of the oral scrapings.  
One exfoliative sample and two biopsy samples were stained for Epstein-Barr virus DNA with a DNA probe.  
The detection of herpetic-type virions by TEM in the keratinocytes of a lesion clinically suspected of being hairy leukoplakia allows a direct and objective diagnosis.  
In addition, the use of exfoliative cytological samples constitutes a simple and non-invasive clinical technique.
